comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral control analyses (C23-C26). Both confirm no significant performance differences across conditions. OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification while peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of objection.

Perfect agreement on representational similarity analyses using Mahalanobis distance (C43-C50). Both support orientation-specific effects of the ping. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the sophisticated use of this metric.

Perfect agreement on methodological details (C114-C121). Both accept sample size justification, power analysis, and ethical procedures without concern. Peer reviewers confirm all methodological concerns were addressed in revisions.

Strong agreement on control analyses (C39-C42, C71). Both confirm ping-induced changes cannot be attributed to sensory information differences or general attentional strength. OpenEval provides detailed statistical support; peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Strong agreement on mechanistic uncertainty (C90-C93, C96). Both acknowledge activity-silent hypothesis as plausible but not definitively proven. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewers accept the framework as reasonable speculation.

Strong agreement on emergence of sensory-like templates post-impulse (C31-C38 overlap with broader R1 claims). Both support region-specific effects and statistical comparisons. OpenEval provides detailed permutation analysis support; peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling.'

Strong agreement on core dual-format finding (C3-C6, C64-C67, C72). Both support the main experimental result showing lack of cross-task generalization without impulse and emergence with impulse. Peer reviewers call this 'compelling evidence' while OpenEval provides detailed convergent support.

Agreement on above-chance decoding and lack of generalization to preparation (C27-C30). Both support non-sensory template during preparation. OpenEval provides detailed permutation statistics; peer reviewers accept as part of overall compelling evidence.

Agreement on neural-behavioral correlations (C51-C55, C52-C55 overlap). Both support meaningful relationship between sensory-like template and behavior. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of between- and within-subject analyses; peer reviewers accept functional relevance.

Agreement on connectivity specificity to preparation period (C61-C63). Both accept information-specific rather than general BOLD changes. OpenEval notes C60's causal interpretation is speculative; peer reviewers accept without explicit concern.

Agreement on enhanced V1-frontoparietal connectivity (C58-C59, C7, C68, C79 overlap). Both support connectivity findings. OpenEval provides detailed statistics; peer reviewers explicitly mention this as accepted evidence.

Agreement on connectivity and behavioral integration (C68-C69, C7-C8). Both support that impulse-driven template has functional consequences for network dynamics. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence; peer reviewers accept as part of flexible template deployment.

Agreement on functional relevance of findings (C69, C8). Both support that sensory-like template has behavioral consequences. OpenEval links connectivity to behavior; peer reviewers accept improved performance association.

Agreement on theoretical framework connecting to dual-template theories (C76-C78, C110, C112, C72-C73, C97). Both support reconciliation of sensory vs. non-sensory debate. OpenEval provides detailed linkage; peer reviewers explicitly state findings 'help reconcile the debate.'

Agreement on theoretical contribution to visual search theories (C76-C78, C98). Both accept connection to existing frameworks. OpenEval notes reasonable inference given functional demands; peer reviewers accept theoretical interest without challenge.

Agreement on V1 regional specificity (C70-C71, C70). Both support stronger effects in V1 versus EVC. OpenEval provides effect size comparison; peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of challenge to regional differences.

Divergence on causal interpretation of connectivity (C79-C80, C60). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative causal claims and trend-level correlation (p=0.086). Peer reviewers accept mechanism without challenge, viewing it as plausible explanation.

Agreement on distinction from working memory (C84, C87, C89). Both accept preparatory attention framework. OpenEval supports with lack of generalization data; peer reviewers accept conceptual distinction as theoretically interesting.

Agreement on literature comparison (C98-C100, C99-C102). Both accept characterization relative to prior work. OpenEval notes accurate representation of consistencies and discrepancies; peer reviewers accept reconciliation of literature.

Agreement on speculative nature of discrepancy explanations (C101-C102, C104, C106, C109). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses require validation. Peer reviewers accept explanations without challenge, suggesting acceptance as reasonable speculation.

Agreement on sustained attention signals (C64). Both accept maintained templates throughout trial periods. OpenEval includes in core finding support; peer reviewers implicitly accept through acceptance of temporal dynamics.

Agreement on functional interpretations being speculative (C9-C10, C73, C113). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting coarse-to-fine transition claims lack direct testing. Peer reviewers accept as part of theoretical contribution to flexible template deployment.
